Python's stdlib `logging` module auto-installs a "handler of last resort" (`logging.lastResort`, a StreamHandler(sys.stderr) at WARNING level) when a logger has no configured handlers and propagation reaches an unconfigured root logger. (2) INDEX-lock contention — '.git/index.lock: File exists' from a live merge-queue git subprocess. To discriminate live-vs-stale before touching it: check whether the lock mtime is advancing AND whether a real git subprocess exists (ps -eo pid,comm,args | awk '$2==\"git\"' — EXCLUDE the claude --print watcher processes, whose --disallowed-tools arg lists literally contain the strings 'git commit'/'git merge', and exclude your own grep). In this session the lock cleared on its own within seconds (it was live), so waiting rather than removing it avoided corrupting a concurrent commit. Never rm a live index.lock.

Reify stdlib joints (crates/reify-stdlib/src/joints.rs) follow this convention: each joint kind is a Value::Map with a "kind" string field plus per-kind data (axis/range for prismatic/revolute; parent/ratio/offset for coupling). Task 1595 (merge_queue: close the rebase-FF-without-reverify main-safety hole — disjoint-delta re-verify gate) shipped 2026-06-01 via commit 67f572601e010ef49c10ed8f81896f21862ddb53.

THE HOLE: advance_main() can succeed via fast-forward when the speculation base is already an ancestor of current main. In that case the speculative verify ran against an older main state; any commits that landed on main between speculation start and advance_main() success were never verified against the merged branch. A branch that breaks mainline tests could slip through.

THE FIX (disjoint-delta re-verify gate): after advance_main() succeeds, compare the post-advance HEAD against the sha that was the verify basis. If `git rev-list verify_basis..new_HEAD` is non-empty (i.e. new commits arrived on main that weren't in the verify basis), the gate forces a full re-verify before the merge is accepted as done. If re-verify fails, the outcome is blocked/failed — not silently merged.

CONTEXT: This fix is part of the shared-core refactor (task 1593). It runs inside the shared post-merge success block, so both MergeWorker and SpeculativeMergeWorker benefit automatically.

In this repo's worktrees, `git diff`/`git show` output is wrapped by a custom pager that strips the `diff --git`/`index`/`@@` headers into a decorative "── file (modified) ──" format — it is NOT a valid unified diff and cannot be fed to `git apply`. Use `git --no-pager diff` (or `git --no-pager show`) to get a real unified diff. This matters when splitting an already-made multi-concern edit into separate atomic commits: extract the header (diff --git/index/---/+++) plus the specific `@@...@@` hunk(s) you want from `git --no-pager diff`'s output into a patch file, then `git apply --cached <patch>` to stage just that hunk (leaving the working tree untouched), commit, then `git add` the same files again to stage the remaining hunks for a second commit.

Gotcha (fused-memory recon_report persistence, task 2716): ReconReportState's reaper clock defaults to asyncio.get_running_loop().time() (MONOTONIC), which restarts near 0 on a fresh event loop. Persisting a monotonic timestamp (e.g. _ReportEntry.completed_at) and restoring it verbatim across a restart breaks TTL eviction: in tick(), now - completed_at goes NEGATIVE against the fresh clock, never exceeds ttl_seconds, so the hydrated completed run never evicts, never quiesces, and store.delete_run never GCs its recon_report_state.db rows — an unbounded leak across restarts. Fix: hydrate_from_store() re-anchors each restored completed_at to self._clock() (in-progress entries with completed_at is None are left untouched, immortal by design; created_at is diagnostics-only and NOT re-anchored). General rule: any monotonic timestamp that is persisted must be re-anchored to the current clock on load, or switched to wall-clock, before it is compared against a fresh-process monotonic clock.

Bash gotcha (reify test-infra): a shell function invoked via the shared `assert` helper (`assert() { ...; if "$@"; then ... }`) runs with `set -e` SUPPRESSED throughout its entire body, because it executes as an `if` condition. Any unguarded `mktemp`/`$()`/`cat` inside such a helper that transiently fails under load will NOT abort — it silently continues with an empty value and can produce a wrong (often spuriously-failing) verdict. Reify GUI test pattern for ResizeObserver in jsdom: jsdom has no ResizeObserver, so tests that need to trigger a resize callback must capture the constructor's callback at construction time. Existing precedent: `gui/src/__tests__/viewport/Viewport.test.tsx:319-350`. Pattern: `let roCallback; globalThis.ResizeObserver = class { observe; unobserve; disconnect; constructor(cb) { roCallback = cb; } } as any;` — render, mock the target's `clientHeight`, then `roCallback!([{ contentRect: { width, height } }] as any, {} as any)`. Restore the original RO in a try/finally so failures don't leak. Same pattern reused for App.tsx side-panel clamp test (96e24a0fb1).

A stateful fake (keying post-restart freshness off a marker the `restart` subcommand touches) lets you exercise both the exit-0 verified path and the failed-verify (exit-1) path — the pattern used for the fleet-deploy clock stamp-on-verified-success recorder tests (task 2396 / I2).
